Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) fell 20.2% between October 9 and October 15, 2026. The decline included an 8.3% drop on October 14 and a further 7.1% drop on October 15. A rapid decline tempts buyers who expect a rebound and who trust the company to keep turning orders for AI systems and traditional servers into sales. So how did people who bought HPE's earlier falls do?

HPE Stock Was Higher A Year After Past Falls

HPE stock has closed more than 20% below its level of 30 trading days earlier on nine occasions since November 2015. Eight of those declines occurred over a year ago, and the stock was higher a year later in every instance. Buyers saw a median gain of 29.5% over that year. The ninth fall took place in November 2025 and remains too recent to judge.

Realizing those gains required patience. In the median case, the stock's lowest close in the following year was 8.6% below its close on the day of the initial fall. After the March 2025 drop, the stock closed as much as 33.2% lower before climbing to be up 17% a year later. The highest price within each year arrived a median 317 days after the decline. Buyers waited about ten months to see that peak.

Is HPE Still Turning Orders Into Sales?

The company is doing just that, though not as fast as customers are ordering. Revenue grew 33.7% from a year earlier in fiscal Q3 2026, which ended July 31, while operating profit expanded even faster. Part of the revenue growth came from HPE's acquisition of Juniper Networks. On management's figures, which count Juniper in both years, networking revenue grew 10%. The operating margin reached 12.0%, compared to 4.7% in the same quarter a year earlier. Cash from operations accounted for 13.4% of revenue, standing close to the 13.2% recorded the previous quarter.

International Business Machines Corporation IBM is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 earnings after the closing bell on Oct. 21. In the quarter, the company is likely to have recorded marginally higher revenues from the Consulting segment driven by rising demand for technology consulting and business transformation services.

Factors at Play

The Consulting segment comprises Strategy and Technology (previously reported as Business Transformation and Technology Consulting) and Intelligent Operations (previously reported as Application Operations). It provides consulting and application management services that offer value and innovation to clients by leveraging industry, technology and business strategy and process know-how.

During the to-be-reported quarter, IBM partnered with India-based artificial intelligence (AI) company Sarvam to develop and test sovereign AI technologies for government agencies and regulated industries in the subcontinent. The collaboration aims to build AI systems that give organizations greater control over data, governance and operations while supporting digital transformation across the public sector. IBM also collaborated with Arm Holdings plc to give enterprises more software choices for mission-critical workloads. IBM's latest processor will enable Arm-native Linux environments to run alongside z/OS and Linux on IBM Z, giving enterprises access to a broader software ecosystem while maintaining security, reliability and scalability. These are likely to have generated additional revenues for the Consulting segment.

In the third quarter, IBM acquired Logiq Consulting, a U.K.-based cybersecurity consultancy, to strengthen its secure digital transformation capabilities and expand its presence across highly regulated industries. The acquisition reinforces IBM's strategy of expanding its cybersecurity portfolio while capitalizing on the growing demand for secure hybrid cloud and AI solutions.

Logiq Consulting brings specialized Secure by Design capabilities, allowing organizations to integrate cybersecurity throughout the technology lifecycle rather than addressing vulnerabilities after deployment. These capabilities complement IBM's existing cybersecurity transformation services and SiXworks' digital transformation expertise in defense and public sector markets. In addition, Logiq's DISX managed sovereign collaboration platform enables government suppliers to exchange sensitive information securely with U.K. government and defense organizations while maintaining control over data management. Integrating these capabilities with IBM's hybrid cloud, AI and consulting expertise could create opportunities for cross-selling services and expanding relationships with security-conscious customers. The buyout also boosts IBM's digital sovereignty offerings as governments and regulated enterprises increasingly prioritize data control, regulatory compliance and operational resilience.

International Business Machines Corporation IBM is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 earnings after the closing bell on Oct. 21. In the quarter, the company is likely to have recorded higher revenues from the Software segment with a strong focus on product innovation and the growing clout of watsonx.ai across various sectors.

Factors at Play

The Software segment includes Hybrid Cloud, Automation and Data and Transaction Processing.

During the third quarter, IBM entered into a multi-year, $240 million agreement with Together AI to support the growing demand for enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) inference. The partnership will enable IBM to expand its cloud infrastructure offerings for open-source AI workloads and strengthen its position in the rapidly growing AI infrastructure market. Under the agreement, the company plans to deploy a large cluster of NVIDIA's HGX B300 systems on IBM Cloud and provide Together AI with enterprise-grade cloud infrastructure powered by NVIDIA's advanced computing and Spectrum-X Ethernet networking technologies.

The deployment is designed to support high-performance AI inference and make large-scale workloads more cost-effective. The collaboration also expands IBM's broader relationship with NVIDIA across AI infrastructure and software. The companies are advancing solutions in GPU-accelerated data analytics, unstructured data processing, hybrid cloud infrastructure and consulting services. These capabilities are expected to help enterprises deploy AI workloads across cloud and on-premises environments with greater performance, flexibility and scalability.

IBM also introduced a new set of AI-powered experiences for the 2026 U.S. Open to make live tennis more personalized, informative and interactive for millions of fans worldwide. By turning complex court-level data into accessible insights, the company helped fans better understand the game through advanced technology. Such investments in innovation and collaborations will likely boost IBM's commercial prospects and are likely to have generated incremental revenues for the Software segment.

In the to-be-reported quarter, IBM collaborated with LTM to strengthen enterprise software supply chain security through AI-driven vulnerability remediation. The partnership aims to help enterprises identify and address vulnerabilities in open-source software while minimizing disruptions to business-critical applications. Per the collaboration, LTM will leverage Lightwell's AI-powered remediation capabilities to help enterprises implement validated software fixes at scale. Building on its long-standing relationship as an IBM Platinum Partner, LTM plans to offer services spanning dependency analysis, risk-based prioritization, DevSecOps integration, testing, validation and large-scale deployment support. The initiative combines Lightwell's software remediation capabilities with LTM's expertise in application modernization, cybersecurity and cloud technologies. The deal is expected to strengthen IBM's position in the enterprise software security market as organizations increasingly prioritize cybersecurity and software supply chain resilience.

title: Stay Ahead of the Game With IBM (IBM) Q3 Earnings: Wall Street's Insights on Key Metrics

Analysts on Wall Street project that IBM (IBM) will announce quarterly earnings of $2.87 per share in its forthcoming report, representing an increase of 8.3% year over year. Revenues are projected to reach $16.84 billion, increasing 3.1% from the same quarter last year.

The current level reflects an upward revision of 0.5% in the consensus EPS estimate for the quarter over the past 30 days. This demonstrates how the analysts covering the stock have collectively reappraised their initial projections over this period.

Before a company reveals its earnings, it is vital to take into account any changes in earnings projections. These revisions play a pivotal role in predicting the possible reactions of investors toward the stock. Multiple empirical studies have consistently shown a strong association between trends in earnings estimates and the short-term price movements of a stock.

While investors typically use consensus earnings and revenue estimates as a yardstick to evaluate the company's quarterly performance, scrutinizing analysts' projections for some of the company's key metrics can offer a more comprehensive perspective.

Bearing this in mind, let's now explore the average estimates of specific IBM metrics that are commonly monitored and projected by Wall Street analysts.

Based on the collective assessment of analysts, 'Revenue- Software' should arrive at $7.62 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +5.7%.

According to the collective judgment of analysts, 'Revenue- Consulting' should come in at $5.35 billion. The estimate indicates a change of +0.5% from the prior-year quarter.

Analysts expect 'Revenue- Other' to come in at $41.75 million. The estimate indicates a change of +9.9% from the prior-year quarter.

The consensus among analysts is that 'Revenue- Financing' will reach $196.75 million. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of -1.6%.

The average prediction of analysts places 'Revenue- Infrastructure' at $3.58 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +0.5%.

It is projected by analysts that the 'Revenue- Intelligent Operations' will reach $2.42 billion. The estimate suggests a change of +1% year over year.

Analysts' assessment points toward 'Revenue- Automation' reaching $1.99 billion. The estimate indicates a change of +4.7% from the prior-year quarter.

The consensus estimate for 'Revenue- Strategy and Technology' stands at $2.93 billion. The estimate points to a change of +1.2% from the year-ago quarter.

The combined assessment of analysts suggests that 'Revenue- Hybrid Cloud' will likely reach $2.07 billion. The estimate indicates a change of +9.2% from the prior-year quarter.

Accenture's $8B Acquisition Push: A Growth Catalyst for ACN Stock?

Accenture plc ACN is stepping up its acquisition strategy, with approximately $8 billion in planned investments for fiscal 2027. The aggressive spending underscores its efforts to strengthen industry expertise, expand into emerging markets and accelerate growth. However, integration challenges could complicate the company's expansion ambitions.

ACN's $8B Acquisition Pipeline

Accenture invested $4.9 billion across 17 acquisitions in fiscal 2026 compared with $1.5 billion across 23 transactions in fiscal 2025. The substantial increase in spending despite fewer transactions highlights its growing appetite for larger acquisitions.

For fiscal 2027, approximately $3 billion of the projected $8 billion relates to Cyber Operational Technology (OT) acquisitions, including Dragos. These transactions shifted from the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 to the first quarter of fiscal 2027 due to regulatory timing.

Management expects to deploy another approximately $5 billion toward acquisitions during fiscal 2027.

Accenture's Inorganic Growth Expectations

Accenture's inorganic contribution to growth was approximately 1.5 percentage points in fiscal 2026, down from 3 percentage points in fiscal 2025.

For fiscal 2027, management anticipates inorganic growth of about 2-2.5 percentage points, highlighting the potential benefits of its expanding acquisition portfolio.

The strategy centers on scaling high-growth businesses, strengthening industry-specific capabilities and entering new growth markets. Cybersecurity-related investments could further enhance its enterprise technology offerings.

What Could Limit ACN's Acquisition Upside?

Despite promising opportunities, substantial acquisition spending carries integration and execution risks. Delays in closing transactions, higher integration costs and weaker-than-expected synergies could weigh on returns.

Accenture's ability to convert its expanding portfolio into sustained revenue growth and stronger profitability will ultimately determine whether its acquisition strategy translates into meaningful shareholder value.

How Do IBM and Cognizant Compare?

International Business Machines Corporation IBM and Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation CTSH are two U.S.-listed competitors pursuing growth through technology investments and acquisitions.

IBM continues to strengthen its hybrid cloud, artificial intelligence, and consulting capabilities through strategic transactions. These investments help IBM address evolving enterprise technology requirements, although integration complexities and competitive pressures remain concerns. IBM's diversified portfolio provides additional growth opportunities.

IBM and Siemens recently announced a research collaboration to advance IBM's nanostack transistor architecture, combining semiconductor research with Siemens' electronic design automation and manufacturing software to improve virtual modeling, design optimization, and fabrication readiness beyond the current 7 angstrom node.

Together with IBM's progress into Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, these projects highlight how the company is committing real R&D resources to chip and quantum architectures that support future AI, hybrid cloud, and high performance computing workloads.

We will look at how International Business Machines' investment narrative is shaped by the Siemens nanostack partnership and quantum milestones.

Scan beyond IBM's nanostack and quantum work to find other chip and compute plays with resilient fundamentals using our curated 32 resilient stocks with low risk scores today.

International Business Machines Investment Narrative Recap

To own International Business Machines, you need to believe that hybrid cloud, Red Hat, AI software and consulting keep driving a higher mix of recurring revenue and steady earnings, even if top line growth runs in the mid single digits. The short term swing factor is still execution around the z17 mainframe and attached software cycle, with macro driven pauses in consulting projects and transactional software demand the clearest threats.

The Siemens nanostack work and DARPA quantum progress matter more for long run compute leadership than for the upcoming quarter. Near term, the key question is whether IBM converts its US$5.5b gen AI book of business and cost actions into the planned free cash flow uplift, while managing scrutiny from the mainframe shortfall investigation.

The DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Stage C selection is the most connected announcement to IBM's semiconductor and nanostack story because it speaks directly to future compute architectures. Independent hardware and systems testing by DARPA gives outside validation of IBM's quantum roadmap, which already supports a network of more than 340 organizations experimenting with scientific and industrial workloads.

For you as an investor, the operational angle is simple. Quantum progress expands the pipeline of high value infrastructure, software and consulting opportunities that sit on top of IBM platforms. Execution risk remains high, and commercial timelines stretch well beyond current earnings guidance, but successful milestones can still support client confidence in long duration AI and hybrid cloud commitments today.

IBM (NYSE:IBM) has paid a quarterly dividend every year since 1916, and 2026 brought its 31st consecutive year of dividend increases. For retired people who own the stock for income, the run matters less than the cash behind it. IBM is also paying for AI, acquisitions and quantum computing, and a weak second quarter has added pressure.

Wright Studio / Shutterstock.com
Free Cash Flow Still Covers the Payout

IBM generated $14.734 billion of free cash flow in 2025 and paid $6.255 billion in common dividends. That means the payout took about 42% of free cash flow. In the first half of 2026, IBM produced $4.8 billion of free cash flow and paid out $3.2 billion in dividends. Management still expects free cash flow to rise by about $1 billion this year. CFO Jim Kavanaugh described the plan on the July call:

IBM poised for modest third-quarter beat, says Bank of America Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America expects International Business Machines Corp (NYSE:IBM), the technology and consulting group, to deliver a modest third-quarter earnings beat on October 21 while keeping its financial 2026 outlook unchanged.

The bank reiterated its 'buy' rating and $280 price target, citing IBM's shift towards higher-margin software, improving profitability and strong free cash flow.

Bank of America forecasts third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion and earnings per share of $2.82, with the potential for a slightly stronger performance from favourable currency movements and profitability.

The bank expects investors to focus on progress in converting delayed deals, signs of a recovery in customer spending and improving growth in Transaction Processing software.

Software growth remains below ideal levels, although Bank of America expects strength in Red Hat (NYSE:RHT)'s OpenShift and Ansible products, alongside continued expansion in the data business following IBM's acquisition of Confluent.

The bank forecasts 4.5% reported software growth for financial 2026, with organic growth, excluding acquisitions, expected to reach 1% for the year as Transaction Processing recovers gradually.

Infrastructure revenue is expected to grow 3% at constant exchange rates in the third quarter, while consulting revenue is forecast to rise 3.6% as growth improves in the second half.

Bank of America describes 2026 as a transitional year for IBM, with a stronger operating performance expected in 2027 as software growth and margins improve.

The bank trimmed its financial 2026 revenue forecast to $70.3 billion from $70.5 billion and its earnings-per-share estimate to $12.40 from $12.45, leaving its price target unchanged at $280.

Its valuation assumes IBM will trade at 19 times the estimated 2027 enterprise value to free cash flow, a measure comparing the company's overall value with the cash it generates after operating costs and capital expenditure.
